title: data-labeling-guidelines-draft-asha-v2
content:
Purpose: This is a working draft of labeling and cleanup guidelines for user-generated text samples. Focus is on clarifying edge cases we keep seeing in the dataset and providing concrete labeling examples for contractors/rotating reviewers. Not final - will consolidate with Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1234) after feedback. Notes / goals: - Reduce labeling variance across reviewers for: intent vs. chit-chat, profanity handling, system/meta text, HTML/snippets, and multi-turn context labels. - Provide deterministic rules so automation (pre-filtering scripts) can be tuned (see linked PR). - Mark obvious clean/skip criteria for ingestion. High-level rules (short): 1) Label at the user-message scope unless otherwise noted. For multi-turn derivations where label depends on context, include both scope_label=USER and context_comment. 2) Prefer single primary_label + optional secondary_tags (max 2). If a sample legitimately maps to two primary intents, pick the dominant user intent and add secondary. 3) Keep profanity handling explicit: LABEL_PROFANITY only if profanity contributes to intent (insult/harassment). Otherwise tag as "contains_profanity" as secondary. 4) System/meta text (eg. "[System] session started" or model tokens) => SKIP if clearly protocol-only. If mixed, label user intent and add tag "contains_system_tokens". Edge cases and examples (concrete): - Ambiguous short utterances: * "Sure" (no context) -> LABEL: chit_chat / ambiguous. Mark as AMBIGUOUS. Dont guess intent. * "Order" (single word) -> LABEL: ambiguous_command. Add tag: needs_context. - Multi-language / code-switching: * "Hola, can you book 3pm?" -> LABEL: scheduling_request, tag: code_switch * Entirely non-English -> LABEL: non_english (unless we have language-specific reviewer). - HTML / markup artifacts in user message: * "
buy now
" -> Strip tags for intent detection: LABEL: commercial_query. Add tag: had_markup. If markup looks injected/malicious, tag: suspicious_html and escalate. - System messages, transcripts, assistant replies included in input: * If message contains assistant reply quoted by user ("Assistant: ..."), label based on the user's explicit request portion. Add tag: includes_assistant_quote. * If file is full transcript including timestamps and system headers with no clear user intent -> SKIP. - Profanity and harassment: * "You idiot, fix this" -> LABEL: abusive_utterance; primary=abuse, secondary=customer_support_request if user also asks for help. * Profanity used for emphasis: "This is f***ing amazing" -> LABEL: positive_sentiment, tag: contains_profanity. Do not classify as abusive if not targeted. - Legal / Privacy sensitive content: * Contains PII (SSNs, emails, phone numbers): redact in downstream storage and tag as contains_pii. Label intent as usual but record pii_tag. Escalate if user asks to share another person's sensitive info. Label taxonomy (proposed short list): - intent_scheduling - intent_commerce - intent_customer_support - intent_qa_fact - intent_chit_chat - intent_command - abusive_utterance - non_english - ambiguous - skip_protocol - data_noise Secondary tags (examples): - contains_profanity - contains_pii - had_markup - code_switch - includes_assistant_quote - needs_context - suspicious_html Sample labeling rows (use for quick training / QA): Raw text | Primary label | Secondary tags | Notes "Hey, what's the weather like tomorrow?" | intent_qa_fact | [] | clear weather query "Your service sucks, refund me" | intent_customer_support | [abusive_utterance] | customer angry + refund request " buy now" | intent_commerce | [had_markup, suspicious_html] | strip markup first but flag "Can you call Mom at 6pm?" | intent_scheduling | [] | scheduling with contact mention (pii?) "OK" | ambiguous | [needs_context] | short response - label ambiguous in most cases Open questions / TODOs (for reviewers): - Should we allow multi-intent primary labels (e.g., intent_customer_support + intent_commerce) or always force single primary? Proposal: single primary + secondary tags to preserve downstream class imbalance. - How to consistently label code snippets that contain human intent vs. purely technical examples. Suggest: if natural language around the snippet expresses intent, label; otherwise tag as data_noise. - PII handling workflow: confirm redaction rules with security/compliance (ticket JIRA-DATA-87). Cleaning heuristics for pre-processing (for engineering): - Remove leading/trailing system markers: regex patterns like "^\[system\].*". If removal changes intent, add tag contains_system_tokens. - Strip HTML tags but record had_markup and suspicious_html if tags contain scripts or event attributes. - Normalize whitespace and unicode before passing to reviewers. Keep original raw text in storage for audits. Reviewer notes / style guide snippets: - When in doubt mark AMBIGUOUS and add a short justification in the reviewer_comment field (contractor UI supports a freeform comment). - Use tags liberally - tags are cheaper to have than wrong primary labels. - Flag any sample that looks like dataset injection or poisoning (repeated patterns, base64 payloads) with suspicious_html or data_noise and notify security. Action items (next steps): - Collect 200 example edge cases from current labeling queue and create a short QA checklist (assigned: Ryan). - Update Confluence page with finalized taxonomy and link to automated pre-filter script PR (assigned: Miguel). - Run a 2-week inter-annotator agreement check on a 1k sample to measure variance (metric: Fleiss kappa). Quick links: CONFLUENCE-1234 | JIRA-DATA-87 | PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-scripts/pull/45 Notes to self: - This doc is messy. Will merge into confluence and remove duplicates. Keep examples visible for contractors. - Remember to sync with security on PII redaction before broadening contractor access. -- Asha
